This family carries, word for word, the sentence the determination names as its proven case: "Any filing fee or fee-waiver answer. No held source states a fee, that filing is free, or a waiver procedure - ask the Criminal Division clerk's office (202-879-1373) before filing." My earlier FAIL demanded a figure the repository does not hold, which is the invention every other rule here forbids; dc_seal_fugitive-set passed on this identical sentence, and a family's terminal state cannot turn on which verifier read it.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Kept on re-examination, and the ground is stated exactly. The instructions never name where the motion is filed: step 4 says "File the motion with the tendered order", which states what accompanies what, and no line says the filing goes to the circuit court clerk or to the county of conviction. The fact is held elsewhere in this repository - the committed legal-design track registry entry for ky_void_seal_controlled_substance states the destination in terms ("Office of the Circuit Court Clerk... filed in the original criminal case in the county of conviction", with the Clerks' Manual filing type recorded) - so this is a fact the build holds and does not carry onto the participant-facing page, and the repair is to state it. Boundary noted rather than decided: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 extends its named-authority reasoning to FEE_AND_WAIVER and SERVICE only, and this packet does name the circuit court clerk for the county in the caption as an authority to ask - about service and about the fee, not about where to file. If Captain extends that reasoning to FILING_DESTINATION, this finding should be revisited; on the determination as written it stands.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Re-examined against DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 and reversed. The packet states that it does not hold the figure and names who does: "The filing fee, and any deadline. Ask the same clerk. No amount and no number of days is stated here, because an unsourced figure in a filing instruction is worse than none." "The same clerk" is the authority named in the bullet immediately above it - the circuit court clerk for the county in the caption - and the caption is one the packet itself fills, so the office resolves to a determinate, reachable clerk rather than a gesture. The stated reason for withholding a figure is the same principle the determination endorses. This obligation no longer contributes to this family's failure.

SERVICE.finding: Re-examined under the determination's extension to SERVICE and reversed. Both halves are delegated to one named, reachable authority rather than left blank. Method: the instructions state the ordinary options and the authority that settles them - "by hand, by first-class mail, or whatever method the clerk tells you this filing requires". The packet is explicit that the order form it is built from does not establish the service rule, which is why it names the clerk instead of inventing a recipient. This obligation no longer contributes to this family's failure.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The repository establishes it and the packet states it. The track registry's destination is 'The county or municipal jail or detention center that holds the booking records ... The written request goes directly to the facility ... No court is involved.' The request's own face opens 'THIS IS A WRITTEN REQUEST TO A GOVERNMENT FACILITY. It is not a court filing; no court, prosecutor or court office receives it', and STEP TWO and STEP THREE tell the participant to identify the booking facility and ask it where a records-restriction request should be sent. The destination is participant-specific by the statute's own design, and the packet names the class exactly and the way to resolve the address.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Met on the third branch of the standard. The packet states plainly that no held source establishes a fee - 'MONEY. No fee is identified for this request anywhere in the records this packet is built from' - and it names a specific checkable authority the participant is already directed to contact before sending: STEP THREE, 'Contact the facility and ask two things: where a records-restriction request should be sent, and whether the facility publishes its own request form.' The facility is reachable in practice and is identified in STEP TWO by the booking that produced the record. This is not the gesture the determination refuses; nobody is told to 'check with the court'. Recorded for the Captain: the MONEY sentence itself names no one, and the authority it relies on is stated two paragraphs above it. I read the standard as addressed to the packet rather than to the sentence, so this passes - but whether the named authority must sit in the same statement as the refusal is a boundary the Captain may want to settle the way A1 settled FILING_DESTINATION.

SERVICE.detail: Met on the first branch: who and by what method are both stated. Who - the facility that booked the participant, at the address it gives; there is no adverse party because no court is involved. Method - 'Certified mail is recommended so you have a record of the date - the facility's 30-day compliance period runs from the request', which ties the method to the statutory clock rather than offering it as etiquette. STEP SIX adds the follow-up at day 31. Nothing is left to be asked of an office the packet does not name.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The strongest in these three lanes. 'WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD' gives three triggers, and 'WHERE TO GO WHEN SELF-HELP STOPS' does not stop at the abstraction - it names four specific desks from the Judicial Council of Georgia's Access to Justice resources: Georgia Justice Project, the Cobb County Second Chance Desk, the Henry County Records Restriction Desk, and Middle Georgia Justice, The Desk. The packet also states what the route never reaches (private mugshot publishers, background-check vendors, non-jail entities, federal and out-of-state records) and prints the O.C.G.A. Sec. 42-8-63.1 caution that a restriction may still disqualify.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The repository establishes it and the packet states it precisely. The track registry names 'The Nevada justice court, municipal court or district court that handled the case, as applicable' and explains that venue follows the court of the underlying case rather than a single court level. The petition caption reads 'IN THE ____ COURT (DISTRICT, JUSTICE OR MUNICIPAL COURT THAT HANDLED THE CASE, AND ITS COUNTY - your own court paperwork states it, and that court's clerk can confirm it)', and the WHERE TO FILE paragraph repeats the rule and its reason. Amendment A1 is satisfied: the packet states the record's answer rather than deferring it.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: The model case for the third branch of the standard, and it does something extra the standard does not require. It states that no held source establishes the fee, with the sources named: 'Neither NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265 nor NRS 176A.295 imposes, authorises or mentions a fee, on either branch.' It refuses to invent an amount: 'this packet states no amount'. It names a specific reachable authority: 'ask the clerk of the court that handled the case before filing.' And it closes off a wrong waiver a participant might otherwise reach for: 'The NRS 179.245(9) sex-trafficking fee waiver is confined by its own words to a petition under NRS 179.245 and is not authority for a waiver here.'

SERVICE.detail: Met on the standard's own terms and stated as carefully as the fee. 'The sections prescribe none: they require only the filing of a petition by the defendant and name no person to be served, while giving the Division the right to object.' It then declines to guess local practice and names the authority: 'Whether your court expects the petition to be served on the Division or on the prosecutor is not established by the text: ask the clerk of the court that handled the case, and follow what that clerk says.' The post-order mechanism is stated separately and sourced - under subsection 4 the court sends the sealing order to each agency named in it, each must notify the court in writing of compliance, and under NRS 179.275 a copy goes to the Central Repository.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Stops are placed where the participant meets them, not only at the end. The branch screen stops a NRS 200.508 or 200.5099 charge cold ('stop: nothing in this packet can be filed'). The discharge-type screen sends an unclear discharge to a lawyer or Nevada Legal Services before anything is filed. The referral page names the two places to go when nothing is filed - the court that supervised the programme, and Nevada Legal Services if the clerk's answer is that no order was entered. A closing list gives five further triggers including a Division objection, which the packet correctly calls a contested proceeding.

recordedDiscrepancyChecked.theReport: A prior lane reported that CO.memo.json still shows this track with build blockers and with destination, filing, fees and service all 'Unresolved', while the 2026-08-28 decision the family binds by SHA resolves every one of them.
recordedDiscrepancyChecked.whatIFound: Confirmed verbatim at this base. data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/CO.memo.json, track co_mistaken_identity_expungement, still carries destination.name 'Unresolved', rules.filing 'Unresolved. The forum and vehicle have not been established.', rules.fees 'Unresolved. § 24-72-702 addresses the costs associated with expunging the record but the section has not been read in full.', rules.notice 'Unresolved.', rules.service 'Unresolved.', two unresolvedQuestions with impact 'build_blocker', legalDesignDecision.status 'legal_research_required', outputStrategyStatus 'unresolved', packetIdentity 'unresolved', and the sentence 'This track is not registered at runtime and is unreachable.'
why: It is stale, not competing. The memo's reviewedAsOf is 2026-07-30; the bound decision is 2026-08-28, a month later, and it answers the memo's own two build_blocker questions in terms — it reads § 24-72-702's mechanism and no-cost rule, records that no dedicated statewide JDF form was located, resolves the output to a custom civil petition with listed contents, and stamps 'LEGAL RESEARCH: COMPLETE'.

It establishes nothing to contradict. Every relevant field says 'Unresolved', which is the absence of an answer rather than a rival answer. A record that answers nothing cannot falsify a packet statement sourced to a record that does.

It is not a held source under A2's list. A2 names the committed TRACK REGISTRY, not the legal-design intake memo — and I checked data/record-clearing/relief-track-registry.json, which contains no co_mistaken_identity_expungement entry at all, so no track registry answer competes either.

It is not the factory's legal-input input. generate.mjs derives legalInputStatus from route-obligation-census-v1/legal-review-queue-v2.json's trueCounselQueue, keyed by routeKey. That queue holds 4 questions, all answered, and none on this route or this track — which is why MASTER_QUEUE records legalInputStatus SETTLED with legalInputBasis null. The memo is not an input to that computation, so this is not a BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT family.

Its runtime sentence is currently accurate, not a false claim: product-wiring.json records DECLARED_NOT_INSTALLED, the field map records generationAllowed false and runtimeSelectable false, and commercialRoutesOpened is 0 everywhere.
recordedDiscrepancyChecked.captainFlag: Purely a records-hygiene hazard, raised not assumed. A stale intake memo asserting 'legal_research_required' and 'build_blocker' sits in the repository beside a built, raster-passed packet. Any future lane that reads the memo before the decision could reasonably reach BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT on a family that is in fact settled. I verify and do not edit records, so this is referred rather than repaired: the reconciliation is to mark CO.memo.json's co_mistaken_identity_expungement track superseded by the 2026-08-28 decision. It changes no obligation and no verdict.

The bound decision establishes the answer outright: 'No filing fee or other expungement cost may be charged', with the product disposition recording 'OUTPUT: CUSTOM NO-FEE DISTRICT-COURT PETITION'. Under A1's test the packet must therefore state it, and it does, three times in the bytes: the petition's own title block ('NO FILING FEE OR OTHER EXPUNGEMENT COST MAY BE CHARGED'), the petition body, and STEP FIVE ('Pay nothing: the recorded rule is that no filing fee or other expungement cost may be charged'). First limb of the standard's `met` list. I also checked the compiled CO profile as A2 requires: its feeRules describe JDF 417, JDF 612 and Clean Slate sealing — different routes, with a waivable fee — and importing them here would both contradict the controlling route-specific decision and breach A2's bar on sibling-route inference. The packet correctly followed the route-specific authority.

SERVICE.detail: The bound decision's serviceWorkflow section is empty and establishes no manner of delivery for this petition. The CO profile's serviceAndNoticeRules are entirely JDF 612 / 'Served on the District Attorney' rules belonging to the sealing routes, which A2 bars me from importing onto a § 24-72-702 mistaken-identity expungement. With nothing in the repository establishing it, a named checkable authority may stand in, and the packet names one for each open point: STEP FIVE 'Ask the district court's office how it accepts filings', and STEP SIX 'Ask the office of the district court how certified copies of the order are obtained.' Third limb of `met`.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Six stop conditions are printed on the packet's own face and each traces to the bound decision: no agency mistaken-identity finding (the decision makes a written request to the agency the first output, not the petition); charges were filed (the decision's precondition is an arrest with no charges); the 90-day deadline has not yet expired (until it does the duty is the agency's); a disputed finding or status (the decision routes disputes to attorney handoff); an attempt to establish innocence where the agency made no finding (the decision: 'not a general vehicle for litigating innocence'); and any immigration question. The instructions also carry 'If a custodian does not act on the order, take the order and your proof to a lawyer.'

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: The packet's pre-filing list omits the one check that decides whether this filing and its two fees are needed at all, and the repository establishes that check for this exact disposition. The compiled Utah state profile carries 'Path B - Automatic Expungement: Acquittal or Dismissal With Prejudice' and, in its own words, 'Acquittal on all charges Goal: 60 days after acquittal for qualifying post-May 1, 2020 cases', together with 'As of January 1, 2026 ... the court identifies and clears eligible automatic-expungement cases on its own'. The same profile carries two questions marked required: true in stage state_specific_eligibility -- source_question_23 '17 Has the case already been automatically expunged?' and source_question_26 'Check automatic expungement. For qualifying post-May 1, 2020 cases, the statutory goal is 60 days after acquittal.' Neither participant-instructions.md nor the delivered canonical bytes contain the words automatic, Clean Slate, 60 days or any equivalent: grep for 'automatic|clean slate|60 day|60-day|120 day' returns zero hits in both. The packet instead directs the participant to pay a non-refundable $65.00 to BCI and $150 to the court. Under A2 the compiled state profile is a held source, and under A3 these lines address this route's own fact pattern -- acquittal -- rather than a sibling statute, so this is not a sibling-route inference. Under A4's widened rule the failure mode is exactly the one named: the packet withholds a fact the repository establishes, and the participant cannot act on it. The repair is to state the automatic route and the check before the fee paragraphs, not to remove the petition route.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both amounts the repository holds are stated, both waiver routes are named, and the one amount that is refused says which amount it is -- which is what A4 requires and is the point this family was re-read on. The court fee: 'The court filing fee is $150', and the delivered cover sheet bytes carry '$150 [X] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)' with the row already selected, confirmed here on packet page 7. The court waiver: form 1305GE, Motion to Waive Fees for Expungement - Criminal, named with Utah Code 78A-2-302 and Code of Judicial Administration Rule 4-508, with the packet saying plainly that the form is not enclosed and naming the clerk and the Utah State Courts self-help forms as where to get it. The BCI application fee: '$65.00' stated in the instructions and confirmed by this lane in the family's own canonical bytes three times -- 'The application fee is $65.00 and non-refundable', 'a non-refundable $65.00 application fee' and 'Application fee is $65.00' on the payment block, all on packet pages 17-18. The BCI waiver: stated, with the sequencing rule that the completed waiver form must accompany the application or it will not be processed, and bci.utah.gov/expungements named as where the form and the Indigent Expungement Applicant Instructions are published; the delivered bytes carry the same instruction and the indigency checkbox. The refusal is narrowed exactly as A4 requires: 'The certificates themselves cost more than the application, and this packet does not state that amount because BCI sets it per applicant' -- it says which of the two BCI amounts it covers, it does not deny stating an amount the packet does state, and it names the Bureau of Criminal Identification as the authority to ask, with the BCI letter identified as where the figure appears. It also warns that the court's waiver does not reach either BCI amount. No A4 breach: the packet nowhere tells the participant that it does not state something it does state.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: participant-instructions.md read in full; pdftotext -layout over fixtures/canonical.pdf, packet page 7 for the selected $150 row and packet pages 17-18 for all three occurrences of $65.00, the indigency checkbox and the waiver sequencing; DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 and amendments A1-A4 read before scoring

SERVICE.finding: The packet states who must receive a copy and by what method, and sources it: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', quoting UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS ('Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'), with form 1146XX Acceptance of Service - Expungement (Prosecutor) enclosed for the acknowledgement and confirmed present at packet page 8. It also tells the participant that the prosecutor or a victim may object, gives the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center number 888-583-0009, and instructs that the service method, address and date be completed only after service actually happens because a certificate of service dated before service is a false statement. That satisfies the obligation as the factory states it. Recorded and referred, not resolved (determination V10-Q1): the route-obligation census for both of this family's route keys says the opposite of the packet on who serves -- 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.' Two committed records disagree. The packet follows the one it quotes and hashes, and the direction of any error is over-service rather than under-service, so this lane did not fail the obligation on it; whether a census record contradicting a bound publication defeats a sourced service statement is Captain's question.
SERVICE.evidence: participant-instructions.md read in full; packet page 8 identified as 1146XX from its own printed heading; route-obligation-candidate.json destination.detail for both ut_pet_acquittal route keys

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: The packet says where it stops. Under 'What this packet is not' it states that this is a prepared set of official Utah forms built for review, that it is not legal advice, that it is not filed for the participant, and that it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement. It also marks the boundary in the specific places it matters rather than only in the disclaimer: it leaves the judicial district and court address to the participant and names the clerk as who confirms them, it refuses to invent the public-interest explanation, it refuses to date a certificate of service before service, and it names the Self-Help Center's phone number for questions about objections and hearings. Scored on this obligation's own terms -- the packet states where self-help ends -- and passing. The automatic-route silence is a distinct defect and is failed under REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING rather than counted twice here, so that a repairer gets one precise instruction instead of two overlapping ones.
SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: participant-instructions.md, sections 'The facts you must supply before filing' and 'What this packet is not', read in full at this base

SERVICE.finding: The service mechanics are right and the objection clock is wrong in a way that can mislead a felony-class petitioner. Correct: two recipients from the form's own Certificate of Service (the prosecuting or city attorney, and the arresting agency), the form's two methods, and the rule that the certificate is completed only after service. The defect is the objection window. The packet leads with a flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object", sourced to the committed packet-set manifest. I traced that sentence: it is data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/AR.memo.json rules.service, and it appears VERBATIM on 11 of the 12 Arkansas tracks in that file — including ar-felony-seal, where the same repository's compiled profile says the window is 90 days. A line that is provably wrong on a sibling track it is attached to is state-level boilerplate, not a route-addressed determination, and under A3 (holding is per FACT, not per document) it does not establish this route's answer. The record that DOES address it is the compiled profile's own table: "Prosecutor objection window - misdemeanor 30 days / felony 90 days, Receipt / filing of petition". That rule is self-applying here, because the delivered petition prints "A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor" and the participant supplies the class. So the repository establishes a determinate class-keyed rule and the packet publishes a flat number from a non-route-held line, demoting the real rule to "the longer window MAY apply to you". It then sends a statutory question to an office that cannot answer it: "ask the clerk of the court where you file which window that court runs" — the window is set by statute, not by court practice, and A1 permits a named authority to stand in only where no held source establishes the fact. The contrast is inside this same builder's own work: ar-misdemeanor-dwi-seal-set resolves the identical conflict correctly by naming its route's class ("this packet is a misdemeanour DWI or BWI conviction, which puts it in the 30-day limb"). The repair is one paragraph: state the class rule as the rule, cite the profile, and drop the clerk sentence. Recorded separately: the three-day service deadline comes only from that same 11-track boilerplate — the compiled profile contains no "three days" and the form prints none — but it errs toward serving early, so I record it as a provenance limit rather than a failure.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Two limbs, and the first is the harder one the Captain asked me to test. (1) The certificate refusal is not merely narrow on this route; it is false, and false in the expensive direction. The packet carries the same paragraph as its conviction sibling, word for word: "The certificates themselves cost more than the application, and this packet does not state that amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The compiled Utah profile records BCI's FAQ as: "eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates may require an additional $65 per case; NO CERTIFICATE ISSUANCE FEE IS REQUIRED FOR DISMISSALS, ACQUITTALS, OR DECLINATIONS." This route is a dismissal. The line is keyed by disposition class and names dismissals expressly, so it is on-route under A3 — unlike the California trap A3 was written for, there is no competing statutory section here, and unlike the West Virginia trap there is no sibling remedy being borrowed. So the repository establishes that the certificate issuance fee is ZERO for this route, and the packet tells the participant it is MORE than $65 and unknowable. That is not a refusal that A1 permits; it is a positive misstatement of a held fact, and it overstates the cost of the route the participant is holding. The identical wording across both Utah families shows why: the fee text was written once for the conviction route and reused unchanged where the disposition class inverts the answer. (2) The free-alternative paragraph omits its own exclusion. The packet tells the participant, in bold, "there is a free route to the same result ... automatic expungement 180 days after the dismissal under Utah Code 77-40a-206, where no appeal was filed", and "If you are not in a hurry, waiting out the 180 days is free." The profile states the carve-out twice, and the packet never mentions it: a dismissal with prejudice following a successful plea in abeyance is excluded from that automatic category. A participant in that position is advised to wait 180 days for relief that will not arrive, having been told their paid petition is merely the faster route to the same end. The disclosure is otherwise admirable — it argues against the packet's own sale — which is precisely why it needs its exclusion.

(1) 'Any offence may fall on the Sec. 100J list, several entries of which turn on facts rather than charge titles' -- carried: the packet reproduces the whole exclusion list. (2) 'Whether every offence occurred before the 21st birthday is unclear' -- carried, first bullet in both the md and the delivered page. (4) 'The district attorney objects' -- carried. (5) 'The court sets a hearing on the best interests of justice' -- carried in substance; the guidance states the hearing rule and 'the determination that expungement is in the interests of justice'. Page ranges read from the canonical bytes: petition 1-5, proposed order 6-8, proof of delivery to prosecutor 9, Statement of Inability 10-21, filing-and-after-order instructions 22-24; 24 pageManifest rows for 24 pages, contiguous. Both conditions are stated with the reason, not just flagged: the proof of delivery ships conditional because Sec. 411.0745(e) makes the COURT responsible for notifying the State while OCA instructions nonetheless direct the petitioner to show proof, so the participant is told to ask the clerk which applies in that county; and the Statement ships conditional because paragraph 6 of the petition is an election between paying and filing it. requiredComponentsMissing is 0 on my own re-run.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: Fifteen writes, and the packet's one-sentence account of them is exactly right against its own bytes -- the only one of the six that is. It says: 'your name on the petition, the proposed order and the Statement, your telephone number on the petition, and your date of birth, address, telephone number and email on the Statement.' reports/actual-writes.json lists 13 form writes plus 2 composed-component writes, and every one falls inside that description: Name1 and Naem2 and Printed Name on the petition, Defendant on the order, and full legal name, date of birth, address, phone and email on the Statement (twice for name and address, since the form asks twice). All 15 were found in the output bytes. The negative claim is also true and I checked it directly: 'Your address is not written on the petition, and that is deliberate' -- page 5 of the delivered canonical shows the Address and City/State/Zip lines empty beneath a filled Printed Name and Telephone Number. And 'Nothing financial is filled in for you anywhere' holds: no financial field on the twelve-page Statement carries ink in either fixture.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: 114 blanks are classified REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and the instructions enumerate them component by component with what to write, across the four documents that carry them. The two documents to obtain first are named with who holds them and why each matters: the Texas DPS criminal history record following DPS form CR-63, which establishes the disposition and every other conviction or deferred adjudication, and the judgment plus the discharge or dismissal order from the sentencing clerk, which establishes which section applies. The deliberately-blank list is specific rather than generic -- the signature and date, everything on the order recording what the State or the court did, the three section boxes, both parts of the address, every financial fact on the Statement, the cause number on the Statement (because its own face says the Clerk's office fills it in when you file), and the district attorney's name and address if that county wants the proof of delivery. knownRequiredFieldsMissing and requiredFactsNotCollected are both 0 on my own re-run.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: Two live elections, both left to the participant or the court, both explained. The OCA order covers Secs. 411.0725, 411.073 and 411.0735 with a box for each, and NONE is marked -- including the Sec. 411.0735 box that is this route's own -- because the printed sentence above them records the COURT's finding, so marking one would assert a finding no court has made. That is the harder and correct call: the route is known, and the packet still refuses, because the box is not a statement of the route but of a judicial finding. The second is paragraph 6 of the petition, the election between paying the fees and filing a Statement of Inability, which is left unmarked and explained, with the Statement shipped so the election can actually be exercised. 44 blanks are classified PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE and requiredOptionsMissing is 0 on my own re-run.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Stated, and stated with the level of specificity the route needs. The heading of participant-instructions.md names it -- 'the Texas court that sentenced you for a misdemeanour' -- and the delivered filing-instructions page tells the participant to call the clerk of the court they are filing in for the mechanics. The committed track registry records the destination as 'The court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, filed through its clerk', with the detail that this is a statewide mechanism with court-level filing and that no county form is promoted to statewide status. The packet matches the registry rather than substituting an authority for it, which is what A1 requires where the repository holds the answer.

evidence.registryDestination: 'The court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, filed through its clerk'

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The best fee handling in this return, and it passes every limb of the determination at once. The delivered page states what the statute actually does -- 'Government Code Sec. 411.0745(b) says the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee THAT [generally applies to the filing of a civil case]... the TYPE of fee, not an amount: there is no flat statutory figure for a petition-based nondisclosure, and your county's civil filing fee schedule governs' -- gives the OCA's figure ('TYPICALLY ABOUT $280'), names the authority to call ('SO CALL THE CLERK OF THE COURT YOU ARE FILING IN and ask what the civil filing fee is'), and then does something no other packet here does: it names the wrong number and disowns it. 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28. You may have read that an order of nondisclosure costs $28... it belongs to [the no-petition route under Sec.] 411.072(c), and the committed record states in terms that it is not a filing fee at all. This is a petition route under Sec. 411.0735. Do not arrive at the clerk's window with $28.' That is A3 applied prospectively against the participant's own likely misreading, not just against a repairer's. The waiver is not merely described but SHIPPED: the statewide Statement of Inability under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, on the form the Supreme Court of Texas approved in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, is component 4, and the registry's rules.feeWaiver names that exact instrument. I verified the fee and waiver text against the registry's rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver for this track and they agree.

evidence.quotedOnDeliveredBytes: 'TYPICALLY ABOUT $280' and 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28'

SERVICE.finding: Stated affirmatively in the direction that protects the participant, with the county variation named and an office to resolve it. The delivered page: 'WHO GIVES NOTICE TO THE STATE - AND IT IS NOT YOU. Under Sec. 411.0745(e), on receipt of your petition THE COURT provides notice to the State and an opportunity for a hearing. The committed record states that you should not be charged for that notice. OCA instructions do direct a petitioner to show proof that the district attorney received a copy, and some counties expect it, which is why this packet includes a proof-of-delivery page marked CONDITIONAL. Ask the clerk whether that county wants it.' That matches the registry's rules.service for this track, which records the same two-limb rule, and the conditional component exists so the participant can comply if the answer is yes. Both limbs of the determination's SERVICE extension are used where each belongs: the rule is stated where the record establishes it, and a named authority stands in only for the county variation no record can settle.

evidence.registryService: 'The court notifies the state. Where local practice requires the filer to deliver a copy to the prosecuting attorney, the packet includes proof that the district attorney received a copy of the petition.'

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: ONE OF THE SEVEN STOP CONDITIONS THE REGISTRY HOLDS FOR THIS TRACK NEVER APPEARS AS A STOP, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MARKS THE MOMENT THE PROCEEDING STOPS BEING SELF-HELP. I compared data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json trackId tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision selfHelpStopConditions against participant-instructions.md and the delivered bytes, condition by condition, grepping each condition's distinguishing terms. Carried: prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence; immigration; the violent-or-sexual determination under Sec. 411.0735(c-1); the Penal Code Sec. 22.01 assault carve-out; and completion of the sentence. ABSENT: 'THE PROSECUTOR OPPOSES THE PETITION OR REQUESTS A HEARING'. The words 'opposes', 'objects' and 'requests a hearing' appear 0 times in participant-instructions.md and 0 times in the delivered canonical bytes; I grepped each. The packet is not silent about the mechanism -- its filing-instructions page says 'A hearing is required UNLESS the State does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice AND the court finds that you are entitled to file the petition and that issuing the order is in the best interest of justice' -- but describing when a hearing happens is not telling the participant that a contested hearing is where they need a lawyer, and the registry names it as exactly that. A pro se participant who reads the 45-day sentence learns to expect a hearing; nothing tells them to stop preparing to attend it alone. RECORDED ALONGSIDE, NOT SEPARATELY SCORED: the registry's first condition is 'Any family violence finding OR FAMILY VIOLENCE ALLEGATION anywhere in the record' and the packet narrows it to 'the court has made an affirmative finding of family violence'; 'allegation' appears 0 times in the md and 0 times in the delivered bytes, so a participant with an allegation and no finding is told nothing, which is precisely the ambiguous case the registry flags. This is the only failing obligation on the strongest packet in this return, and the repair is two bullets.

Repeating-row groups were computed by importing the repository's own rowKeyOf rather than by pattern-guessing, specifically to avoid the known failure in which statutory numerals inside identifiers are parsed as row-group counts. All six families produced 0 row groups; no spurious group appeared from 1017_1019, 1017a, 1018, 19c or 12-60.1-02.
vfdRead.nineZeroCountersAreNotAVerdict: All six families read PASS_COMPLETE with all nine completeness counters zero, and three of the six carry a real defect anyway. Each obligation row names the instrument that measured it.
